system_overview: This specification models a distributed replicated log system inspired by the Confidential Consortium Framework (CCF). Multiple servers each maintain their own copy of an append-only log. Servers can extend their logs with new values and copy missing entries from other servers. The specification demonstrates how the finite monotonic technique can be used to find violations of liveness properties, specifically showing that full synchronization (all logs identical) is not guaranteed even under fairness.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of servers, each maintaining its own log, and a finite set of possible values that can be appended to logs. A constant parameter controls the maximum allowed divergence (lag) between any two servers' log lengths.
state_variables: The system tracks a mapping from each server to its own local log, represented as an ordered sequence of values. Each server's log grows independently but is bounded in how far it can diverge from other servers' logs.
initial_state: All servers start with an empty log (a sequence of length zero).
actions: There are two types of transitions: (1) Copy: a server whose log is shorter than another server's log copies a suffix of entries from the longer log to its own. The number of entries copied is close to (but may be slightly less than) the full difference in log lengths, specifically between one less than the difference and the full difference. This means a copy operation may not fully catch up the lagging server. (2) Extend: a server whose log is at least as long as every other server's log appends new values to its log. The number of new entries appended is bounded so that the resulting lag between the extending server and the shortest-logged server does not exceed the lag parameter. This action is only enabled for servers that currently have the longest (or tied for longest) log.
safety_properties: Bounded lag: the absolute difference in log lengths between any two servers must never exceed the lag parameter. Type correctness: all logs remain sequences of valid values.
liveness_properties: All extending: every server must always eventually strictly extend its log (make progress). This property is verified to hold. In-sync: all servers should always eventually have identical logs. This property is demonstrated to NOT hold -- the model checker correctly finds a counterexample because copy operations are allowed to transfer only a partial suffix, so a follower may never fully catch up.
model_bounds: The lag parameter, server set, and value set are declared as constants. The lag must be a natural number and the server set must be finite. For model checking, typical values are three servers, one value, and a lag of three.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for both the extend and copy actions for every server. Unlike the CRDT and replicated log examples, this specification has a machine-closed fairness constraint. However, it makes the unrealistic assumption that a server can consistently read the state of all other servers, which would not hold in a real distributed system where messaging protocols would be needed to determine lag between servers. The specification relies on community library modules for sequence and finite set extensions.
